rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods / Results sections - the study reports its own laboratory filtration experiments (six filtration cycles with two recycled-glass media, reclaimed wastewater), with its own TSS retention measurements and OCT image analysis (Tables 3-5, Figs 5-6).
rows.notes: The study is a laboratory methodology paper on using optical coherence tomography to quantify particle fouling across the depth of a pressurised media filter used in drip irrigation systems with reclaimed wastewater. It contains no crop, no yield, no field data, no climate or environmental comparison, and no result on the effectiveness of drip irrigation for crop production varying with crop type or environmental conditions. The only mention of drip irrigation and crop-related benefits is in the Introduction citing other work (Ayars et al. 2007). The claim is not supported by any result of this study; the subject matter (filter fouling assessment) is a different technology/component from drip irrigation effectiveness on crop yield.

notes: Full text appears complete (Introduction through Conclusions); reference list and tables/figures content not included but not needed. The study is wholly unrelated to the cited claim about drip irrigation effectiveness on crop yields varying with crop type and environment.
